land.text: the Loango district on the coast, the seat Buali (Mbansa Loango)

predecessors.note: The infobox lists the Kingdom of Kongo as predecessor: the founder's home district Kakongo was 'itself a vassal of Kongo' and Duarte Lopes wrote in 1585 that the king of Loango 'was a vassal in past times'. Phyllis Martin argues Loango was already independent in 1535, because Afonso I's titles then named Kakongo, Vungu and Ngoyo but not Loango.

successors.note: The infobox names French Congo as successor; the French Congo page dates its formal establishment to 30 November 1882 and its confirmation to the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885.

The History of Angola page (opened for the portuguese-angola dossier): the Cabinda territory was ceded to Portugal 'under a protectorate treaty concluded between the Portuguese Crown and the princes of Cabinda in 1885'; the Loango page itself does not mention Cabinda's fate.

capitals.name: Buali (Mbansa Loango)
capitals.note: APPROXIMATE: the coordinates are the gazetteer's Loango (Republic of the Congo), standing in for the royal town; the page gives the capital as 'Buali (or Mbansa Loango)' without coordinates.

correction.text: the Loango district on the coast, the seat Buali (Mbansa Loango)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Loango): the page dates the state 'c. 1550' and gives no area; the first kingdom is drawn as the district around Loango (confidence low).

correction.text: 'from Cape St Catherine in the north to almost the mouth of the Congo River', in 'the western part of the Republic of the Congo, Southern Gabon and Cabinda'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'at its height in the 17th century' the kingdom reached 'from Cape St Catherine in the north to almost the mouth of the Congo River'; the page gives no area and no year for the height, so the union of Kouilou, Pointe-Noire, Niari, Cabinda and Nyanga is a reading (about 68,000 km2) held to 1883. After the death of King Buatu in 1787 'no king was elected for over 100 years', which the page does not tie to any loss of land.

region.text: the Loango district on the coast, the seat Buali (Mbansa Loango)

ledger.note: c. 1550: the Kingdom of Loango, a state 'created by Kongo people', appears on the coast (infobox 'Established: c. 1550'; Phyllis Martin dates an earlier foundation to 'the late fourteenth or early fifteenth centuries'). The page gives the district's name, not a boundary.

region.text: 'from Cape St Catherine in the north to almost the mouth of the Congo River', in 'the western part of the Republic of the Congo, Southern Gabon and Cabinda'

ledger.note: 17th century: the kingdom reaches its height. 'At its height in the 17th century' it extended 'from Cape St Catherine in the north to almost the mouth of the Congo River'. The page dates the height only to the century; 1600 is the bridge year (confidence 1).

region.text: 'from Cape St Catherine in the north to almost the mouth of the Congo River', in 'the western part of the Republic of the Congo, Southern Gabon and Cabinda'

ledger.note: c. 1883: Loango ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 1883', 'succeeded by French Congo'; the text says only that 'Loango ceased to exist during the 1800s'. The French Congo page: 'formally established as the French Congo on 30 November 1882', confirmed at the Berlin Conference of 1884-85.

certainty.note: A coastal trading kingdom with no surveyed boundary; the 1884-1885 borders with Cabinda and the Congo Free State were set by treaties that neither page dates.

notes: Cliopatria has no Loango. The page names no area, boundary, treaty or war; the French Congo page does not mention Loango except in the infobox, so the end is c. 1883 on the Loango page's word alone. Not settled: the Vili vassal kingdoms Kakongo and Ngoyo (not on the page as Loango's), the Portuguese Cabinda protectorate (Treaty of Simulambuco, not on either page), Mayumba, the French treaties of 1883-1885. The capital is the gazetteer's Loango as a proxy. Gazetteer names: none missing. Page budget (2-5): two pages, the second thin.
